title: Health Insurance Amendment (Extended Medicare Safety Net) Bill 2009

divisions.question: That this bill be now read a second time. That the amendment ( **Senator Cormann’s** ) be agreed to.

speeches.speaker: Penny Wong
speeches.brief: The bill amends the Health Insurance Act to allow the Minister to set maximum benefits under the Extended Medicare Safety Net (EMSN) for selected MBS items, saving over $450 million over four years. It argues that unlimited EMSN benefits have enabled some doctors to inflate fees, with 78 cents of every EMSN dollar going to higher charges rather than reducing patient costs, and caps will apply to obstetrics, ART, hair transplantation, eye injections, varicose vein treatment, and cataract surgery.

speeches.speaker: Rachel Siewert
speeches.brief: The Australian Greens argued the bill fails to address rising out-of-pocket health costs and would place the burden on vulnerable patients, particularly those needing IVF and cataract surgery, and therefore they could not support it. An opposition senator also opposed the bill, citing that it would increase costs for IVF and cataract patients, and moved a second reading amendment to delay consideration until final regulations were available.
Senator Cormann moved an amendment to delay further consideration of the bill until three sitting days after the final regulations and determinations are tabled.

speeches.speaker: John Faulkner
speeches.brief: The opposition argued the government's changes to the Extended Medicare Safety Net, particularly for IVF, would increase costs for families and broke a pre-election promise, while the government defended the caps as necessary to control excessive doctor fees and keep the safety net sustainable. The bill was passed after the government tabled final regulations that restructured IVF items, which the opposition said needed more scrutiny.

speeches.speaker: Mathias Cormann
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the bill broke the Rudd government's promise not to reduce the Medicare safety net, leading to higher out-of-pocket costs for patients, particularly for IVF, obstetrics, eye surgery, and macular degeneration treatment. He announced that non-government senators forced a backflip on IVF-related items and successfully passed an amendment requiring future determinations to be approved by both houses of parliament.
